title: Mara and the Harvest
premise: Mirabel Zhou, a pest controller who moved to the village of Hollowmere to disappear after a courtroom failure that haunts her, is called to investigate noises in the church vestry—noises that leave handprints in the dust. The bell that rings each dusk was melted down in 1911, and its tolling marks the return of the founders' unfinished harvest ritual, which requires a descendant of the families who broke their covenant to complete it. Mirabel learns she is the last heir of the Zhou line that settled Hollowmere and abandoned the rite mid-ceremony, leaving the village's dead to walk hungry. To end it, she must finish the ritual herself—an act of justice the law never delivered—sacrificing her anonymity and nearly her life, but freeing both the dead and her own buried guilt.
about_author: Tamsin Ravensworth is the pen name of a former rural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing parish records in the English fenlands. Their fiction blends folk horror with quiet domestic dread, and they write exclusively at night, when the bells are quiet.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A routine pest-control call to St. Brannoc's ends with Mirabel finding human fingerprints in the vestry dust—at shoulder height, pressed into plaster. She tells herself it's vagrants, but takes the job anyway because the fee is good. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking five years of practiced denial.

chapters.title: Bell Weather
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At dusk the church bell rings; the parish register confirms it was melted for scrap in 1911. Villagers don't react—they've always heard it. Old Mrs. Ellery grips Mirabel's wrist and says, 'It knows your name now.' Emotional beat: the first crack in Mirabel's rational armor.

chapters.title: What the Register Kept
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, intercut with 1911 diary fragments from founder Edmund Zhou. In the county archive Mirabel finds the founders' covenant: seven families bound to an annual harvest rite, broken mid-ceremony by her own ancestor. Emotional beat: inheritance as indictment—the past isn't behind her, it's addressed to her.

chapters.title: Handprints
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The prints multiply nightly, now on her own cottage walls, always at the height of someone kneeling. She sets traps and cameras; footage shows nothing but the prints appearing between frames. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into obsession—she stops sleeping to watch.

chapters.title: The Seven Families
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. She tracks descendants of the other six founders; two have vanished recently, three refuse to speak, one—a boy named Colm—confesses his family has fed the thing at the lychgate for generations. Emotional beat: complicity everywhere; the village's normalcy revealed as maintenance of a lie.

chapters.title: Lychgate
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Following Colm's directions, she witnesses the offering: bread and blood left at the gate, taken by something with too many joints. It wears her ancestor's face. It says, 'You were supposed to finish.' Emotional beat: confrontation with the personal made monstrous.

chapters.title: A Justice of Her Own
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, flashback-heavy. The novel's core wound surfaces: the trial where Mirabel's testimony failed to convict the man who destroyed her family, and why she fled to Hollowmere. The entity offers her what the court wouldn't—his name, his location, his debt. Emotional beat: temptation; justice outside the law dangled like bait.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Rite
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel with Colm. Deciphering Edmund's diary, they reconstruct the interrupted ceremony: the founders fled at the moment of naming, leaving the harvest unclaimed and the dead unbound. The rite must be completed by a founder's blood before the final bell on All Hallows' Eve. Emotional beat: grim resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: All Hallows' Eve
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. In the ruined crypt beneath the tower, Mirabel begins the rite as the dead converge. The entity offers again—her enemy's ruin in exchange for walking away. She refuses the bargain and speaks the naming instead, claiming the debt as hers. Emotional beat: climax; choosing costly justice over easy vengeance.

chapters.title: After the Tolling
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The bell falls silent forever; the prints fade; the dead are released. Mirabel, scarred and no longer invisible, stays in Hollowmere—not hiding now but keeping watch, teaching Colm the covenant's true terms. Final beat: quiet resolution; identity accepted, justice rendered, the harvest finally gathered.
